key_insight: Quantum reinforcement learning enables musical agents to develop distinct compositional behaviours through reward-driven interaction rather than large-corpus imitation.
engineering_relevance: A hybrid quantum–classical framework connects parameterised quantum circuits with MIDI-based workflows for adaptive computer-aided composition and performance.
method: Represent musical agents as parameterised quantum circuits updated through reinforcement learning.
Use atomistic agents for separate pitch and rhythm decisions, or holistic agents for unified pitch–duration events.
Combine and weight musically grounded rewards to shape distinct agent mindsets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports generalisation to unseen musical material, interactive and offline MIDI demonstrations, and musically meaningful learning on IBM quantum hardware, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish a quantum advantage over classical reinforcement learning or quantify scalability on current hardware.
paper_title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
